sentences.en: He said, quote, the moral panic about leftism on universities is largely their fault, referring to fire here.
sentences.zh: 他说，引用他的话，“关于大学左倾的道德恐慌很大程度上是他们的错”，这里指的是FIRE（个人权利与表达基金会）。

sentences.en: What do you make of that accusation?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待这种指责？

sentences.en: And do you feel any responsibility for laying the groundwork for what we've seen now?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得为我们现在所看到的一切奠定基础负有任何责任？

sentences.en: Now, if I believe that there wasn't a grave problem in higher ed that was very, very real, if I felt like, oh, my God, I exaggerated it, I didn't exaggerate it.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果我相信高等教育中不存在一个非常、非常真实的严重问题，如果我觉得，哦，天哪，我夸大了它，我并没有夸大它。

sentences.en: This was a very real thing that people were responding to.
sentences.zh: 这是一件人们正在回应的非常真实的事情。

sentences.en: And my point has always been, I've been doing this for 25 years.
sentences.zh: 我的观点一直都是，我已经做这件事25年了。

sentences.en: If you'd listened to us 15 years ago, there wouldn't have been this kind of excuse just laying at your feet for the Trump administration to pull.
sentences.zh: 如果你15年前听了我们的建议，就不会有这种借口摆在特朗普政府面前让他们利用了。

sentences.en: So, like, the idea that the person who is warning you and even saying things like, this is going to create a right-wing backlash.
sentences.zh: 所以，那种认为警告你的人，甚至说出“这会引发右翼反弹”之类的话的人，

sentences.en: And it's created a right-wing backlash.
sentences.zh: 而且它确实引发了右翼反弹。

sentences.en: And I think people who would rather me not have said anything over the last 25 years are saying that I should apologize for what I said, but I'm not about to do that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为那些宁愿我过去25年什么都没说的人，在说我应该为我说过的话道歉，但我绝不会那样做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You're saying the calling out is a necessary thing for you and for the culture in general.
sentences.zh: 你是说，大声疾呼对你和整个文化来说都是必要的事情。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I want to return to this idea of creating a culture of free speech and to the benefits of creating that kind of culture.
sentences.zh: 我想回到创造言论自由文化这个想法，以及创造这种文化的好处上来。

sentences.en: Because earlier in our conversation, you laid out this dynamic where if you air bad ideas, ideas that people find repugnant,
sentences.zh: 因为在我们之前的谈话中，你提出了这样一种动态：如果你公开糟糕的想法，那些人们觉得令人反感的想法，

sentences.en: they will get exposed in the public square and eventually many people will turn on them because of that exposure.
sentences.zh: 它们就会在公共广场上被曝光，最终许多人会因为这种曝光而反对它们。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, though, if that is always true, because what we're seeing right now is this debate that's happening about platforming people with hateful ideas.
sentences.zh: 不过，我想知道这是否总是正确的，因为我们现在看到的是关于是否允许持有仇恨思想的人发声的辩论。

sentences.en: I'm thinking specifically of the conversation around avowed white nationalist Nick Fuentes being invited onto Tucker Carlson's podcast recently.
sentences.zh: 我特别想到的是关于最近邀请公开的白人至上主义者尼克·富恩特斯（Nick Fuentes）参加塔克·卡尔森（Tucker Carlson）播客的对话。

sentences.en: And the question that's being asked is, does platforming someone like Fuentes just allow those ideas to reach a broader audience and gain purchase with more people?
sentences.zh: 人们提出的问题是，给像富恩特斯这样的人提供平台，是否只是让这些想法接触到更广泛的受众并获得更多人的认同？

sentences.en: Does it just normalize those ideas rather than chasing them off the public square?
sentences.zh: 这是否只是让这些想法正常化，而不是把它们赶出公共广场？

sentences.en: Because as far as I can tell, the platforming of someone like Fuentes has only brought him more into the mainstream.
sentences.zh: 因为据我所知，给像富恩特斯这样的人提供平台，只会让他更进入主流。

sentences.en: It hasn't actually hurt his popularity.
sentences.zh: 这并没有真正损害他的人气。

sentences.en: There's this kind of straw man version of the argument for free speech, which is that all you have to do is let speech be as free as possible and everything will work out great.
sentences.zh: 关于言论自由的论点有一种稻草人版本，那就是你所要做的就是让言论尽可能自由，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: We think freedom of speech is a necessary precondition to human rights.
sentences.zh: 我们认为言论自由是人权的必要前提。

sentences.en: And for that matter, knowing the world as it is, it's necessary, but it's not sufficient to addressing the ills of the world, but it is a minimum condition.
sentences.zh: 而且就此而言，了解世界的本来面目，它是必要的，但不足以解决世界上的弊病，但它是最低条件。

sentences.en: If we're going to be a democratic society, we can't hate the people so much that we can't trust them to hear things and come to conclusions.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想成为一个民主社会，我们就不能如此憎恨人民，以至于我们不能信任他们去倾听事物并得出结论。

sentences.en: You know, like that's not a free society anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那就不再是一个自由社会了。

sentences.en: That's a paternalistic or maternalistic society.
sentences.zh: 那是一个家长式或母权式的社会。

sentences.en: Like the goal of the free speech defender is to get us off the seesaw of who gets to censor who.
sentences.zh: 言论自由捍卫者的目标是让我们摆脱“谁有权审查谁”的跷跷板。

sentences.en: Now, what does that mean for platforming?
sentences.zh: 那么，这对提供平台意味着什么？

sentences.en: I do actually think that hopefully we can have a society where someone can have someone odious on their show, you know, ask them questions,
sentences.zh: 我确实认为，希望我们能拥有一个社会，在那里有人可以在他们的节目中邀请令人厌恶的人，你知道，问他们问题，

sentences.en: and we don't assume that those ideas spread like viruses into other people's brains.
sentences.zh: 而我们不会假设这些想法会像病毒一样传播到其他人的大脑中。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of times we think that just by shutting this person up or by not actually anyone being allowed to hear from them, that's solving the problem.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为很多时候我们认为，仅仅通过让这个人闭嘴，或者不让任何人听到他们的声音，就能解决问题。

sentences.en: But there's group polarization research that essentially, if you just get people to talk to the people they already agree with,
sentences.zh: 但有群体极化研究表明，本质上，如果你只是让人们与他们已经同意的人交谈，

sentences.en: they tend to get more radicalized in the direction of the group.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会朝着群体的方向变得更加激进。

sentences.en: Whereas if you have people talk to people they disagree with, it works better.
sentences.zh: 而如果你让人们与他们不同意的人交谈，效果会更好。

sentences.en: Even, Greg, in a world where people are really only listening to people they agree with, where these media environments are so siloed, you still think that's the case?
sentences.zh: 即使，格雷格，在一个人们真的只听他们同意的人说话的世界里，在这些媒体环境如此孤立的情况下，你仍然认为情况是这样吗？

sentences.en: I think that sometimes in the effort to sort of fix problems with humanity, we think if we can just shut the right people up, these problems are going to go away.
sentences.zh: 我认为有时为了解决人类的问题，我们认为如果我们能让正确的人闭嘴，这些问题就会消失。

sentences.en: And it never, ever works.
sentences.zh: 但这从来、从来没有奏效过。

sentences.en: You know, after talking to you, it seems pretty clear that the value of free speech is something that both sides, the right and the left, claim.
sentences.zh: 你知道，和你谈过之后，很明显言论自由的价值是左右两派都声称拥有的东西。

sentences.en: And then you have seen over the course of your career that they also don't always practice what they preach.
sentences.zh: 而且你已经在你的职业生涯中看到，他们并不总是言行一致。

sentences.en: And you've given us this defense of free speech that is actually, for me, it's been uniquely personal.
sentences.zh: 你给了我们这种对言论自由的辩护，对我来说，它非常个人化。

sentences.en: You've couched it as something that is really important to one's personal mental health and also therefore important to a society's general health.
sentences.zh: 你把它描述为对一个人的个人心理健康非常重要，因此对社会的整体健康也很重要的事情。

sentences.en: And I wonder if that's part of the argument that you would make about why it's essential to democracy.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否是你论证它为何对民主至关重要的部分原因。

sentences.en: Or what you would say about why it is so worth preserving.
sentences.zh: 或者你会说为什么它如此值得保护。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, you're not a free people if you don't have free speech.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，如果你没有言论自由，你就不是一个自由的民族。

sentences.en: It's as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单。

sentences.en: And people who are in favor of censorship, they really are telling you don't be yourself.
sentences.zh: 而那些支持审查制度的人，他们确实是在告诉你不要做你自己。

sentences.en: They're really saying don't be authentic.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是在说不要真实。

sentences.en: Lie if you need to betray what you actually believe.
sentences.zh: 如果需要的话就撒谎，背叛你真正相信的东西。

sentences.en: And even if they think they're doing it for the absolute best reasons in the world, and usually they do.
sentences.zh: 即使他们认为他们这样做是出于世界上最好的理由，而且通常他们确实是这样认为的。

sentences.en: In most of human history, the censors, they think they're on the side of goodness and right.
sentences.zh: 在大多数人类历史中，审查者认为他们站在善良和正义的一边。

sentences.en: And sometimes I can understand why they would think that.
sentences.zh: 有时我可以理解他们为什么会那样想。

sentences.en: But ultimately, so many times when you're looking at threats to freedom of speech, they are about be less of you, be less of who you are, be less authentic.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，当你审视对言论自由的威胁时，它们往往是关于：少一点你自己，少一点你是谁，少一点真实。

sentences.en: And if there's weird things going on in your head, don't tell anyone for God's sakes.
sentences.zh: 如果你的脑子里有奇怪的想法，看在上帝的份上，别告诉任何人。

sentences.en: So I do think that there's that aspect of autonomy that's represented in free speech I think is deeply personal to all of us.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为言论自由中体现的那种自主权对我们所有人来说都是非常个人化的。

sentences.en: But then there's the informational part of it, just the knowing the world actually as it is.
sentences.zh: 但随后还有它的信息部分，仅仅是了解世界的本来面目，

sentences.en: because you simply cannot know what your society looks like if everybody's afraid to say what they really think.
sentences.zh: 因为如果每个人都害怕说出他们真实的想法，你就根本无法知道你的社会是什么样子的。

sentences.en: Well, Greg, thank you so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，格雷格，非常感谢你的时间。

sentences.en: It has truly been fascinating to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 和你交谈真是太迷人了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I really enjoyed it, too.
sentences.zh: 我也很享受这次谈话。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: During a classified briefing on Thursday, members of Congress watched a video of the controversial airstrike
sentences.zh: 在周四的一次机密简报会上，国会议员观看了一段有争议的空袭视频，

sentences.en: that killed two alleged drug smugglers who clung to a boat in the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 那次空袭杀死了两名据称在加勒比海紧抓着一艘船的毒品走私者。

sentences.en: That airstrike in September, a follow-up to an initial attack on the boat, is now the subject of an inquiry by the Senate and House Armed Services Committee.
sentences.zh: 那次9月份的空袭，是对最初攻击那艘船的后续行动，目前正受到参议院和众议院军事委员会的调查。

sentences.en: But after viewing the video, Democrats and Republicans had starkly different impressions of what had happened and whether it violated the rules of war.
sentences.zh: 但在观看视频后，民主党人和共和党人对所发生的事情以及它是否违反战争规则有着截然不同的印象。

sentences.en: What I saw in that room was one of the most troubling things I've seen in my time in public service.
sentences.zh: 我在那个房间里看到的是我在公共服务期间看到的最令人不安的事情之一。

sentences.en: you have two individuals in clear distress without any means of locomotion with a destroyed vessel who are killed by the United States.
sentences.zh: 你有两个处于明显困境中的个人，没有任何移动手段，船只被毁，却被美国杀害。

sentences.en: Democratic Representative Jim Himes of Connecticut suggested the video showed the military killing shipwrecked sailors who posed no threat.
sentences.zh: 来自康涅狄格州的民主党众议员吉姆·海姆斯（Jim Himes）表示，视频显示军方杀死了对他们不构成任何威胁的遇难船员。

sentences.en: But after watching the same video,
sentences.zh: 但在看过同一段视频后，

sentences.en: Republican Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas said it appeared to be a lawful attack.
sentences.zh: 来自阿肯色州的共和党参议员汤姆·科顿表示，这看起来是一次合法的袭击。

sentences.en: I saw two survivors trying to flip a boat, load it with drugs, down for the United States, back over, so they could stay in the fight.
sentences.zh: 我看到两名幸存者试图把船翻过来，装上毒品，运往美国，然后再折返回来，这样他们就能继续战斗。

sentences.en: And potentially...
sentences.zh: 而且可能……

sentences.en: Meanwhile, The New York Times has sued the Pentagon for infringing on the First Amendment rights of journalists
sentences.zh: 与此同时，《纽约时报》起诉了五角大楼，称其侵犯了记者的第一修正案权利，

sentences.en: by imposing a new set of restrictions on reporting about the military.
sentences.zh: 因为五角大楼对有关军队的报道施加了一系列新的限制。

sentences.en: Those restrictions, which cover a wide range of journalistic activities, are contained in a 21-page form that the Defense Department has required reporters to sign
sentences.zh: 这些涵盖了广泛新闻活动的限制措施，包含在国防部要求记者签署的一份21页的表格中，

sentences.en: in order to keep their Pentagon press passes.
sentences.zh: 以保留他们的五角大楼记者证。

sentences.en: Many news organizations, including The Times, have refused to sign the form.
sentences.zh: 包括《纽约时报》在内的许多新闻机构都拒绝签署该表格。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。
